transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Thank you for seeing me. I'm here because my sense of whether I’m doing well or not has started to revolve almost entirely around what I weigh and how tightly I’m controlling my shape. It has become the main metric I use to judge myself every day.
Have you been intentionally restricting your food intake to lose weight, or do you mainly worry about your weight and shape without actively dieting or restricting?

I am actively restricting, though I view it more as being disciplined and efficient rather than standard dieting. Most days I just have black coffee, maybe a yogurt or apple in the afternoon, and a tiny salad for dinner. I get incredibly anxious even thinking about eating things like pasta or sandwiches, so keeping my intake this tight is how I manage that worry.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight, or is your weight currently still in the normal range despite the restriction?

I have lost a significant amount of weight, to the point where my clothes are hanging off me and my sister keeps telling me I look "frail." My primary care doctor was also very alarmed by the drop at my last exam, but personally, I don't see it as worrisome and still feel like I could stand to tighten up a bit more.
Do you feel a strong fear of gaining weight, and do you see yourself as overweight even when other people say you are too thin?

Yes, the fear of gaining weight is very intense; even thinking about eating pasta makes me anxious that it will show up on my stomach the next morning. And despite my sister saying I look frail and my clothes hanging off me, when I look in the mirror, I still feel I could stand to tighten up a bit more.
Have you ever had episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short time and then trying to get rid of it by vomiting, using laxatives, or excessive exercise?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that or tried to purge. My pattern is actually the exact opposite, where I strictly restrict what I eat—often just having coffee, an apple, or a small salad—and skip meals to maintain control and avoid gaining weight.
Have you had any medical symptoms from the weight loss or restriction, such as fainting, feeling cold all the time, missed periods, or slowed heartbeat?

I don't experience any of those symptoms and actually feel completely fine. I'm still highly active, walking miles through hospitals for my sister's care and working full days, which is why my doctor's warnings about potential heart issues or bone loss seem quite overblown to me.
Have you had any changes in your menstrual periods, such as missing periods for three months or more, since the weight loss began?
That isn't really applicable to me anymore. I am 63 years old and went through menopause quite a few years ago.
Do you believe your self-worth depends mainly on your weight and shape, or do you feel that other parts of your life and identity matter just as much?

Yes, my sense of success or failure has become almost entirely dependent on whether the scale has ticked down and if I've stuck to my food rules. Other important areas, like my consulting work or how well I'm caring for my sister, don't really register anymore when I evaluate my day. It almost all comes down to how tightly I'm controlling my shape.
At your current weight, would you say you are underweight for your height, or has your weight stayed in the normal range despite the restriction?

My doctor and sister certainly insist that I am underweight and look "frail," but I don't see it that way at all. I feel completely fine, active, and disciplined in my routine. When I look in the mirror, I just feel like I could stand to tighten up a bit more rather than seeing anything to worry about.
Do you think your current weight is too low, or do you still feel you need to lose more weight even though others say you are underweight?

I don't think my weight is too low at all, even though my sister says I look frail and my clothes are hanging off me. When I look in the mirror, I still feel like I could stand to tighten up a bit more. Because I still have the energy to work and walk miles, I see myself as just being disciplined rather than dangerously underweight.
Do you believe your current weight is too low, or do you still feel you need to lose more weight even though others say you are underweight?

I really don't think my weight is too low, even if my sister says I look frail and my clothes are hanging off me. When I look in the mirror, I still feel like I could stand to tighten up a bit more. Because I have plenty of energy to work and walk miles, I see my weight as a sign of discipline rather than anything dangerous.

She denies binge eating or purging. This is most consistent with anorexia nervosa, restricting type.
